completion_promises.criterion_text: Grep invariant test (#6) uses pathlib.Path.rglob + str.contains to scan src/jarvis/ for hard-coded subject literals; allow-list documented in the test docstring.
completion_promises.evidence: TestNoHardcodedSubjectLiteralsInSrc uses _iter_source_files() which calls _SRC_JARVIS.rglob('*.py') (pathlib.Path.rglob) and `forbidden in content` / `forbidden in line` (str.__contains__) to scan src/jarvis/ for the three forbidden literals 'agents.command.', 'agents.result.', 'fleet.register'. The class docstring documents the four-rule allow-list: (1) module/function docstrings, (2) comment lines, (3) nats_core.Topics import lines, (4) lines that reference Topics.* templates rather than emitting literals.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Tests fail loudly if any subject string is hard-coded (failure message names the offending file + line).
completion_promises.evidence: test_no_hardcoded_subject_literals_in_src walks each line, records offenders as f'{rel}:{lineno}: {line.strip()}' (relative path + line number + line content), and asserts `not offenders` with a multi-line message naming each offender. The assert message is 'Hard-coded subject literal {forbidden!r} found in src/jarvis/ outside the allow-list (...): \n' followed by the joined offender list — every offending file:line shows up in the failure output.
